newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr to pause, then test key supports.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr to pause, then test key supports.

text.p: The dollar is likely to trade sideways until the meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee on Tuesday and it may resume its slide afterwards, chartists said on Friday.

The FOMC is meeting on Tuesday as the marketplace is about equally divided regarding the future level of the 5.50-percent federal funds rate. About half of the 39 U.S. primary dealers expect a 25-basis-point hike and the other half no move.
Regardless of the FOMC decision, traders said the dollar could be vulnerable to a new selloff since the policy outlook beyond that meeting would remain uncertain.
In New York on Friday, the dollar closed at 115.65/75, off from 115.75/85 yen on Thursday, and at 1.6920/30 marks, down from 1.6965/70.
Technical analysts said the 114.65/70 level -- the low on Thursday -- was an important support level that, if broken could lead to a slide to the 110 to 109.30 area.

"We broke some major channel lines on dollar/yen this week. The 110-yen level is very possible, it's a valid target over the next two months," said senior analyst Chris Turner at the consultancy firm I.D.E.A., who saw no sign of a real recovery in dollar/yen since the fall from 127.45 on May 1.
Dollar/mark looked firmer, though confined to a trading range between 1.6850 and 1.71 on the near term, technical analysts said.

"The big levels for dollar/mark are 1.6850 to a certain extent, and more so 1.6780, a trendline from last November's lows that held last Monday when we fell aggressively," Turner noted. "There may be some large corrections coming up in dollar/mark, but they have not been confirmed yet."
Turner said some support lines were converging on dollar/mark, meaning "the risk/reward suggests you should be buying dollar/mark on the dips."
Dollar/Swiss looked bearish and may lead the way down versus the European currencies, predicted Turner who saw "a key support line at 1.4120 Swiss at the moment."
"But if 1.38 Swiss goes, things would look very bad for the dollar," Turner added.
But Turner also noted mark/Swiss "tested a very big level at 83.75," that, if lost, would be favorable for the dollar.
Analysts also said cable may have more strength in store and that only the loss of $1.63 would mark the end of the rally.
